script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for September 10. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
A tapeworm lives in your gut, eating your food, giving nothing back.  A tick drinks your blood and leaves.  Parasitism is the dark side of relationships—one organism benefits while the other pays.

In parasitism, value flows one direction. The parasite gains; the host loses. This differs from symbiosis where both gain. Direction of value flow reveals relationship type. The best parasites aren't obvious—they extract just enough to benefit without killing the host.  Some human relationships work the same way: slow drains that persist unnoticed.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Not all relationships are mutual.  Some extract value without return.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Balance Check - Give and Take Audit.

Here's your activity: Pick a relationship—personal or professional. Track what flows each way: energy, support, resources, opportunities. Is it balanced? If not, is that temporary or chronic? Address chronic imbalances before they drain you—or before you drain others. This helps you identify imbalanced relationships.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about living off others can be applied to balance check - give and take audit. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
